findings.existing_code: A principal may report only its own `agent_id`; trust-level 3 operators may report another lane.
findings.description: The principal-binding model introduced in revision 2 is inverted relative to who actually observes rate limits. D7 says the reporters are the shared result collectors in review_dispatcher.py and provider_dispatch.py, which run under the ORCHESTRATING session's key (e.g. claude-local) and report the DISPATCHED lane (e.g. grok-local, codex-remote). Every real dispatcher report is therefore a cross-lane write and is only permitted for trust-level 3 principals. agents.yaml binds *-remote lanes and cloud-harness identities to trust_level 2 (claude-remote:104, codex-remote:183, grok-remote:347), so any orchestrator running under those keys receives 403 for every observation and the registry never learns from cloud runs; the 'Principal reports own lane' scenario almost never occurs in practice. The spec needs an authorization rule that matches the producer topology (e.g. a principal may report any lane it is configured to dispatch to, or a dedicated vendor_registry.report operation checked via authorize_operation), and the wp-api-watchdog 403 tests must encode that rule rather than own-lane-only.
findings.resolution: Replace own-lane-or-trust-3 with an explicit reporter-authorization rule tied to dispatch capability or a policy-engine operation; keep anti-spoof binding of source_agent_id to the principal; add a scenario for a trust-2 orchestrator reporting a lane it dispatched.

findings.existing_code: The coordinator image SHALL package the reused health probe so deployed watchdog runs cannot silently skip it.
findings.description: Packaging the probe file is necessary but not sufficient, and the 'Deployed probe' scenario (spec.md:89-92, 'present and executable') passes while producing zero snapshots. Two deployed-path defects remain: (a) watchdog.py:409-417 resolves the probe at Path(__file__).parents[2]/skills, which in the image (/app/src/watchdog.py) is /skills/..., whereas the Dockerfile sets SKILLS_ROOT=/app/skills (Dockerfile:115) and github_classifier.py already honours that variable; (b) vendor_health.load_agents_yaml (vendor_health.py:110-155) finds no roster in the container unless AGENTS_YAML is set (no ENV in Dockerfile) or COORDINATION_API_URL points back at itself, so check_all_vendors returns an empty report and every lane stays 'unknown'. With D9's default fail-closed posture and D4 rule 5, an all-unknown registry silently halts automatic switching in production. The plan must require SKILLS_ROOT-based resolution and an explicit roster path, and the deployed-probe gate must assert at least one snapshot is written, not just file presence.
findings.resolution: Amend D1/task 3.6 to specify SKILLS_ROOT lookup and roster path injection; strengthen the Deployed probe scenario to 'produces >=1 snapshot in the production image'; add the probe path to scripts/check_docker_imports.py data-dir checks.

findings.description: wp-roadmap-policy must inject a 'registry provider' into orchestrator.py (spec Registry-Driven Roadmap Policy; D9 requires distinct timeout/auth/not-found/server/malformed provenance), and the only repository-native place those normalized list/availability reads are defined is the bridge (D6). Those helpers are written by wp-dispatch-reporting, a parallel sibling (both depend only on wp-api-watchdog), and coordination_bridge.py is outside wp-roadmap-policy's write_allow. orchestrator.py currently imports no bridge module (orchestrator.py:13-64). The package either blocks on an artifact it cannot see, or duplicates an HTTP client with its own error taxonomy, violating D6's single-convention intent.
findings.resolution: Add wp-dispatch-reporting to wp-roadmap-policy.depends_on, or split the bridge read helpers into a package both consumers depend on.

findings.description: D4 collapses a model-scoped limit into lane-level `limited`, contradicting the dispatcher behaviour the plan builds on: review_dispatcher.py (752-890, 1274-1300, 1537) treats a capacity error on one model as per-model and falls back to standard/economy tiers on the same lane. Under D4, the first opus-tier 429 reported with scope=model marks the whole lane limited, so available_only reads and roadmap policy exclude a lane that is still dispatchable on fallback models while the dispatcher keeps using it. Neither spec nor OpenAPI defines when a model-scoped limit affects lane status or whether per-model limits are informational only.
findings.resolution: Define model-scope semantics: lane status becomes limited only for scope=lane, or when all configured models are limited; otherwise expose model limits in rate_limits without changing lane status, and document how policy consumes them.

findings.existing_code: AND the limited lane SHALL be excluded before grouping by provider.
findings.description: The in-run switching rule assumes the limited identity is a lane, but the only producer of roadmap outcomes is the prompt layer (autopilot-roadmap SKILL.md, outside every write_allow), which emits vendor_limit:<policy_vendor>:<reason> (orchestrator.py:90,135,1033-1036) with no lane. D7 correctly makes persistence skip as ambiguous, but the policy path is undefined for this common case: when only policy_vendor is known, does policy exclude every lane with that policy_vendor, none, or fail closed? Excluding none would re-select a sibling lane of the same limited provider (claude-remote after claude-local), which usually shares the quota; excluding all is the sensible legacy-compatible behaviour but is not stated, so tests in 5.1 cannot be written deterministically.
findings.resolution: State that a provider-only limit excludes all lanes whose policy_vendor matches for the current decision (without persisting), record that widening in decision provenance, and add a scenario.

findings.existing_code: Existing static tiers may rank degraded candidates but SHALL NOT populate `expected_cost_delta_usd` or enforce a USD ceiling.
findings.description: Revision 2 correctly removes static tiers from USD enforcement, but a catalog quote is computed only when dispatch context supplies an exact catalog model plus prompt/completion token estimates, and no package, task, or interface produces those estimates (PhaseDispatchPayload in provider_dispatch.py:30-40 has no token fields; roadmap dispatch context carries none). Net effect: cost_ceiling_usd (policy.py:240-256), enforced today via static tiers, becomes a silent no-op for every user who set it. The plan should either name the estimate producer and heuristic, or define the posture when a ceiling is configured but the quote is unknown (fail closed vs proceed with an explicit provenance warning), plus a migration note for existing roadmaps.
findings.resolution: Add a scenario 'ceiling configured, quote unknown' with a defined action and provenance field; name where token estimates originate or state that ceilings are advisory until dg-04.

findings.existing_code: The existing watchdog SHALL persist every lane probe snapshot, including the first baseline
findings.description: The reused probe only evaluates lanes with a cli section (vendor_health.py:164-167), and grok-remote deliberately has none (agents.yaml:344-362). 'Every lane' is therefore unsatisfiable as written: grok-remote never gets a vendor_probe_state row, stays unknown under D4 rule 5, and is permanently excluded from available_only reads and from roadmap candidates under the default posture, despite having a coordinator identity and archetypes. The plan should state how lanes without a probe method are represented (explicit snapshot with status=unknown and reason=no_probe_method, or a documented exclusion). Round-1 consensus id 35 raised this; revision 2 covers local lanes via the catalog gate but not non-CLI cloud lanes.
findings.resolution: Define a 'no probe method' snapshot or an explicit exclusion rule, and add a scenario covering a configured lane without cli/endpoint evidence.

findings.description: Task 6.2 requires Ruff, mypy, migration, contract, DAG, and strict OpenSpec gates, but wp-integration's verification steps are pytest x2, openspec --strict, and ruff x2 only. mypy (the coordinator's documented gate is mypy --strict src/), the migration applier, a contract-parity re-run against the merged tree, and the work-package DAG/scope validator are not executable steps, so the tier-A package cannot evidence what the task list promises. Round-1 ids 23/40 concerned the absence of any test gate; that is closed, but the remaining named gates are still not executable.
findings.resolution: Add verification steps for mypy --strict, the migration check, re-running test_vendor_registry_contracts.py, and validate-packages DAG validation, each with result_keys.

findings.existing_code: Expired rows are omitted from reads and compacted after a seven-day audit-retention window.
findings.description: Compaction is specified as a behaviour and tested in task 2.3, but no component owns running it in production: neither the watchdog (the coordinator's only periodic worker), a migration-time job, nor an API-triggered sweep is assigned, and no work package or task names the trigger. Without an owner the retention bound is aspirational and the (agent_id, reset_at) index grows unbounded, reopening round-1 id 44 in practice.
findings.resolution: Assign compaction to the watchdog loop (or a named scheduler) with an interval config key, and add it to wp-api-watchdog scope and tests.

findings.existing_code: using existing authentication headers and existing status/result/error conventions.
findings.description: The spec simultaneously mandates the existing bridge normalization and requires not-found to be preserved as a distinct error. The existing convention (coordination_bridge.py:477-482) maps every 404 to status=skipped, reason=capability_unavailable, which for the registry conflates 'coordinator lacks the /vendors routes' with 'unknown lane' (the 404 that GET /vendors/{agent_id}/availability and the POST return for a bad agent_id). The plan should state how the two 404 meanings are distinguished (e.g. by response detail code) or explicitly accept the conflation for reads while treating POST 404 as a hard reporting failure.
findings.resolution: Define the 404 disambiguation rule for registry operations in D6 and a bridge test for it.

findings.existing_code: CoordinatorApiKey: {type: apiKey, in: header, name: X-API-Key}
findings.description: D6 states all routes accept Bearer, X-Coordinator-API-Key, or X-API-Key (matching verify_api_key at coordination_api.py:593-612), but the OpenAPI document declares only Bearer and X-API-Key. Contract-parity tests in wp-contracts will therefore not exercise the X-Coordinator-API-Key path that the CORS-facing UI uses.
findings.resolution: Add a third securityScheme for X-Coordinator-API-Key and list it in the top-level security array.

findings.description: D4 rule 2 gates local lanes on 'non-stale available matching catalog model', but CatalogModelPrice projects only price, refreshed_at, and stale; the catalog available flag (model_catalog.available, catalog.py:38) is not surfaced. A consumer seeing a local lane as unavailable with a fresh catalog row cannot tell from the response which model failed the availability gate, undermining D10's explainability goal.
findings.resolution: Add available: boolean to CatalogModelPrice so local gating is explainable from the read model.
